scope: Read-only comparison of unchanged Nemu0.7,0.7a and target native code. No compiler probes, binary patching or new source reconstruction.

author_note.interpretation: The release note says the resampler was rewritten and separately announces a High Quality setting. Native calls distinguish those changes: the setting selects an envelope mixer, while opcode5 uses the new resampler regardless.

0.7.algorithm: Q16 linear interpolation between adjacent signed16-bit PCM samples: a + (((b-a)*(phase &65535)) >>16). Pitch is doubled, count gains16 speculative samples, then phase is rewound by16 pitches before saving state.
0.7.history: Eight saved input samples plus a fractional phase, loaded/stored through five byte-swapped32-bit state words.

0.7a.algorithm: Q15 phase;64 fractional positions; four signed16-bit coefficient/PCM products; arithmetic shift15; saturation to[-32767,32767].
0.7a.history: Four main samples at state[0..3], phase at state[4], signed extra-history count at state[5], and up to seven continuation samples ending at state[15]. Flags1 resets; flag2 restores continuation history.

current_target.algorithm_and_state: Same four-tap Q15 algorithm and history protocol as0.7a. Command words are already byte-swapped; PCM storage is reached through context->buffer rather than embedded in context.
current_target.reference_scan_limitation: This establishes no direct entry references in the image, not proof of reachability for every possible computed address.

high_quality_switch.reason: The surrounding command handler100010A0 loads input/output/count and all three auxiliary buffers. The selected call belongs to envelope mixing; the scalar-resampler call sites do not read this switch.

coefficient_identity.storage: Both kernels are in writable .data. The raw coefficient identity and transformed layout do not uniquely determine the original declarations.

corresponding_native_regions.operation: phase normalization, fractional index and convolution

prior_source_ancestry.observation: The linear interpolation, eight-sample state, sixteen extra outputs and phase rewind appear in the older0.7 routine. This historical source does not supply the later four-tap implementation.

behavior_diagnostic.adaptation: Only command byte order and context layout change: embedded historical PCM buffer and fields at220c/221c/221e versus a current buffer pointer and fields at14/24/26. Both original x86 bodies and coefficient bytes execute unchanged.
limitations: Finite synthetic vectors do not establish equivalence for every input or recover source spelling.
No candidate compiler output or patched machine code is executed.

recovery_implications: The target scalar routine is a retained descendant of the0.7a rewrite, not a direct translation of UltraHLE linear resample.
Its history protocol, signedness, scaling, saturation and coefficient ordering now have independent historical native evidence.

Different native product scheduling does not uniquely prove an explicit four-term expression versus an unrolled source loop. Both forms were already exercised in the176 current scalar controls; this evidence alone does not justify repeating them.
